The home citation (anf05:544, 'And lastly we have Novatian as a sequel...') is Coxe's editorial introduction, not Novatian.

why: The count passes and his own works are held, but Novatianism grew from his consecration (founder), so it is Mark's question.

name: Constantius II

rejected.nikodemos-hagiorite_synaxaristes-vol2-ma: same paragraph as 4789 (Life of Cyril of Jerusalem)

findings.what: The recommendation's stated grounds should change. By the letter of the rule he qualifies. Two later traditions whose shelves legitimately hold Nikodemos (Ottoman 1650-1821, Kollyvades) reach 5 and 7. He has words of his own in the strict sense: a document issued in his name, the letter to the princes of Auxumis, given verbatim in Athanasius. And he founded nothing. 'Home not settled' is no reason to hold: the census lists him in two movements, and the draft's choice of the Homoian one is sound. The real objection is that every counted passage comes from one author's single work, the Synaxaristes, shelved under nested traditions. That is a reading of the rule, so it belongs to Mark.
findings.evidence: npnf204_athanasius-select-works-letters.xml:36143-36144 (div 18.2.31, 'Letter of Constantius to the Ethiopians'); census homoian-arian-christianity and gallic-nicene-episcopate people rows
findings.fix: Keep hold, but put the reason as one question for Mark: does a single author's work, shelved in two nested traditions, meet 'two traditions'? Drop 'home not settled'.

findings.what: The parish-millet shelf (1453-1650) holds Nikodemos's Synaxaristes (written c. 1805, printed 1819), more than 150 years after the tradition ends. Any count under that shelf from these volumes is formally valid but anachronistic. This is a shelf defect to register; it should not be relied on as a counted tradition.
findings.fix: Count only Ottoman 1650-1821 and Kollyvades. Register the shelf assignment as an open gap.

findings.what: vol2 14645 sits in a note block (wider lines before the page number 124), presumably Nikodemos's own footnote rather than a modern editor's. It counts, but it is the weakest of the five.

why: He passes the rule, but only through one author's work under two nested traditions. That question is Mark's, and it should be put as such, not as a home problem.

findings.what: Fails the count, so consolidated 'passes: true' is wrong. All sixteen counted refs are Malech's Persia chapter (lines 10364-13001), outside both rows' loci. Timur's other shelved work (Mai X, Ebedjesu's collection with Timothy II's synod) names Mar Aba in only 3 distinct passages. The draft gives Chaldean 'clean 0', but Badger vol. 2 (whole file on the Chaldean shelf) names him as 'Mar Awa' in five distinct passages. Four are in Ebedjesu's catalogue (Appendix A, a translated primary text): the liturgy translated by Tooma and Mar Awa, Mar Awa the Great translating the Old Testament, his disciples, and the list of Eastern synods. why: He meets every other test (documents in his name, no movement founded), but only one later tradition (Chaldean, via Badger) reaches five passages; Timur stops at three.

name: Gregory VII

findings.what: Bengel 21177 uses 'Hildebrand' as a byword (Zosimus 'whom some call an early Hildebrand'). It refers to Gregory VII only by figure. The count holds without it: the German file names him in body text at 31538, 31585, 32393, 34195 and others.
Notes of the Church 14580 is the tract quoting Bellarmine's own list of saints (in guillemets), so the words are Bellarmine's. It still counts; Restoration has 9 without it anyway.
The movement carries his name ('Gregorian Reform'), which could raise the founder question. But the census dates it from Leo IX's circle around 1049, before his pontificate, so he is not its founder.

why: Documents in his own name are held (Mirbt no. 235), he founded no movement, and Pietism (6) and the Restoration Church of England (9) name him in their own texts.

name: Huldrych Zwingli

findings.what: Three of the five Huguenot passages (120333, 120437, 121494) are not a Huguenot's words. They lie in John Jewel's 'Apologie de l'Eglise d'Angleterre' (running head from 116705 to 124963), reproduced whole in Crespin's Book XI. The draft's quote is from it, and it is presented as a French Huguenot naming Zwingli. They are inside the row's locus, so the count stands by the letter of the rule. If Mark rules that a whole work by an outside author embedded in a shelved book does not count, the Huguenots fall to 3 (Crespin 11383, 79725; Beza 35110) and the candidate fails.
findings.fix: Change the quote to Crespin 11383 or 79725 ('mise en auant depuis cinquante ans par Luther, apres lequel est venu Zwingle'). Name the Jewel dependence in doubts.

findings.what: Beza's Histoire ecclesiastique I names 'Luther, Zvingle & Calvin, heresiarques' in a decree it quotes. That is a sixth Huguenot passage outside Jewel. The other Beza hits are the Baum-Cunitz editors' notes.
Shakers 17041 and 17054 are quoted Mosheim, inside the Testimony. They count; the other four are the Shakers' own narrative.

why: His own works are held, but the Reformed Cities entry begins with his Zurich reform (founder question for Mark). The Huguenot leg also leans on Jewel's Apology.
